title: —On “Godot” pronunciation:  @Joe Weinberg  —On Jamie Lloyd + Celebrit...
transcript: here are my honest thoughts on Keanu Reeves and Alex Winter in this Broadway revival of Waiting for Godot directed by Jamie Lloyd obviously these two actors famously starred together in the Bill and Ted franchise and now they're reuniting on Broadway to take on one of the most iconic plays in the canon first thing I'll say is that I really enjoyed studying the work of Samuel Beckett in school but seeing his work perform live out in the world has generally been less satisfying and enjoyable for me but I will say this was one of the most watchable Samuel Beckett productions I've seen Jamie Lloyd directs it so that the tone shifts throughout the play are a little bit more pronounced which I think helps break up some of the monotony and gives it a better sense of pacing and in general I would say there's a lot about Jamie Lloyd's direction that I liked naturally this play that's set in a desolate liminal space unmoored in time is kind of right in his wheelhouse the big problem for me and this is a big problem is that I just I don't think Keanu Reeves and Alex Winter were that good AND/OR I don't think Jamie Lloyd adequately tailored the production to their strengths I actually thought they did a pretty good job during the more playful, clown-like physical comedy sections especially in Act 2 but too often they just seemed a little bit out of their depth in general I thought Alex Winter was somewhat better than Keanu Reeves and both of them were outshined by the actors playing Pozzo and Lucky I didn't really buy them as two characters who had been lost in this purgatory for uncounted time I felt a lot of the time like they were play-acting what they *thought* Waiting for Godot should be like rather than just of bringing themselves fully to the role and I do kind of blame Jamie Lloyd for that too this production was conceived around these two actors who are known together as this comedic duo and that is where their strengths lie and it's frustrating I guess that Jamie Lloyd wouldn't play into those strengths or direct it around those strengths even though like I said I liked what he did with it on its own terms I know this sounds absolutely insane but I honestly think this production might have made more sense if they had just performed it in their Bill and Ted voices I did a whole video earlier this year which I'll link in the caption theorizing that part of the reason so many celebrities like working with Jamie Lloyd is that he incorporates their celebrity identity into the work he doesn't ask the audience to pretend that they're someone else he embraces that relationship and allows it to fuel the storytelling and the interpretation of the material and there were times in the play where I felt that one very obvious moment in particular but also because I was looking for it there were times when I was reflecting on the nature of their relationship and their relationship to the public as it related to the situation of these characters but overall I don't think they did that sufficiently or holistically here and I'm being a little bit facetious when I say they should have just done the show as Bill and Ted but only kind of cause I genuinely think it might have grounded them a bit more and made them feel more at ease in the text so overall I would say I enjoyed this production more than not I enjoyed watching it but I think the specific way in which they missed the mark was very frustrating given the nature of the production
